The Interior · Costa Paradiso, Sardinia

Interior

The defining feature of the villa's interior is a full-height panoramic window, opening onto the Mediterranean Sea and the granite coastline of Costa Paradiso. The living room is arranged so that the sea becomes a natural part of the interior, and the changing light of the day fills the house with its own particular atmosphere.

Living Room

A Wall of Glass, Framing the Sea

In front of the panoramic window is a seating area, its sofa dressed with cushions and a throw in natural silk that bring a sense of comfort and Mediterranean ease. Beyond the glass, a hand-forged wrought-iron balcony railing frames the view — its scrollwork echoing the ironwork found throughout the property.

Terrace & Garden

An Outdoor Room Above the Sea

The villa is wrapped by a generous terrace that extends into a private garden. Strawberry trees, myrtle and fig grow here, while large planters of aloe vera underline the southern character of the residence. Sheltered by rock and by carefully trimmed shrubs, the garden holds an atmosphere of complete seclusion.

Layout

Three Levels, One Open Heart

The house unfolds across three levels. At its centre is a large hall, opened into the kitchen as a single continuous space — the two areas divided not by a wall but by a hand-forged iron partition, a detail that keeps light and sea view moving freely through the room.

From the living room, a staircase rises toward the sleeping quarters. Its steps are faced with hand-painted Sardinian tile, and the kitchen wall carries the same handcrafted ceramic character.

Bedrooms

Two Bedrooms, Two Bathrooms, a Door to the Garden

The layout includes two bedrooms and two bathrooms. One bedroom opens directly onto the garden, where an outdoor shower, a laundry area and a storage room are arranged. Along one side, an external staircase, built into the natural slope of the site, follows the contour of the land.

Art in the House

The Paintings of Nona Dronova

Original art holds a special place in the interior. Every room is hung with paintings by Nona Dronova, devoted to flowers and Mediterranean gardens. The paintings draw the interior of the house into conversation with the surrounding landscape and give the villa its individual character.

Materials

Turquoise Wood, Ceramic and Mediterranean Light

The furniture is made of solid wood, painted in a deep turquoise that echoes the tones of the sea beyond the panoramic window. This combination of natural materials, handcrafted ceramics, original painting and Mediterranean light shapes an interior in which architecture, nature and art exist as a single whole.

At a Glance

Interior Highlights

  • Full-height panoramic window facing the sea
  • Hand-forged wrought-iron balcony railings
  • Three-level villa architecture
  • Hall and kitchen united, divided by a hand-forged iron partition
  • Private garden with strawberry trees, myrtle and fig
  • Hand-painted tile on the staircase and kitchen wall
  • Direct garden access from one of the bedrooms
  • Paintings by Nona Dronova throughout the house
  • Solid-wood furniture in turquoise
  • Two bedrooms and two bathrooms
